mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% within a month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE crosses above 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) over two months signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise >0.10% and >0.3% respectively over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise by the specified thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both > 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during coordinated GDPC1 and HOUST surges above 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals labor market strength, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS is persistently above its 12-month MA for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reliably produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month MA for six consecutive months.
